facts.statement: The genus Rhombodus was first described by Dames in 1881.
Rhombodus is classified as a prehistoric ray within the family Rhombodontidae.
facts.quote: Rhombodus is a prehistoric genus of ray belonging to the family Rhombodontidae.

facts.statement: Species of Rhombodus lived between 70.6 and 55.8 million years ago, spanning the late Cretaceous and early Paleocene.
facts.quote: Species within this genus lived from the Cretaceous period, Maastrichtian age to the Paleocene epoch, from 70.6 to 55.8 million years ago.

facts.statement: Individual Rhombodus species could grow to a length of 75 to 100 centimeters.
facts.quote: Rhombodus species could reach a length of 75 - 100 cm.

facts.statement: The genus is primarily known from fossilized caudal spines and rhombic teeth.
facts.quote: This genus is known from its caudal spines and rhombic teeth, which are all that usually fossilises.

facts.statement: The rhombic teeth of Rhombodus are bilobate with vertical wrinkles and measure about 1.5 cm in width.
facts.quote: These rhombic teeth are bilobate, with vertical wrinkles and a width of about 1.5 cm.

facts.statement: The time range for Rhombodus extends from the Santonian to the Thanetian, approximately 85.7 to 56 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Thanetian (85.7 to 56 million years ago)

facts.statement: Rhombodus belongs to the class Chondrichthyes.
There are 126 recorded fossil occurrences of Rhombodus in the Paleobiology Database.
Fossils of Rhombodus have been found in sedimentary rocks across Africa, Europe, Asia, and the Americas.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found in the sediments of Africa, Europe, Asia and the Americas.
